labeler: blind independent review, generic OWASP rubric, no knowledge of the tool under test
notes: Canonical Vercel reference SaaS starter (Next.js 14 + Supabase + Stripe). Reviewed for the common Supabase/Next.js footguns and found none worth flagging: (1) schema.sql enables Row Level Security on EVERY table (users, customers, products, prices, subscriptions) with correct owner-scoped policies (auth.uid() = id / user_id); the private 'customers' table has RLS enabled with NO policy, i.e. fully locked down; the only 'using (true)' policies are SELECT-only on the intentionally public product/price catalog. (2) The service_role key (utils/supabase/admin.ts) is used only in server modules and is accompanied by an explicit warning comment; it is never imported into client code. (3) The browser client (utils/supabase/client.ts) uses NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY only. (4) The Stripe webhook (app/api/webhooks/route.ts) verifies the signature via stripe.webhooks.constructEvent before processing. Deliberate non-finding: .env.local.example line 4 contains a JWT-looking anon key, but it is the universal Supabase LOCAL-DEV demo anon key (iss=supabase-demo, pointing at http://127.0.0.1:54321) and anon keys are public by design; a competent reviewer does NOT flag it. Included as a precision test case: a scanner that flags this repo is producing false positives.
